route: exemption: explicit code labels in the paper (S1 Appendix AT1-AT3) + route 1 (published per-item loadings and reliabilities, Table 2)
evidence: Route is the printed-code-label exemption, corroborated by route 1. (A) Wang & Zou's S1 Appendix (10.1371/journal.pone.0346229.s001, DOCX) prints the attitude block as three labelled lines -- 'AT1-Using DG technology is pleasant.', 'AT2-I find using DG technology to be enjoyable.', 'AT3-I have fun using DG technology.' -- so all 3/3 shipped item_text strings reproduce the appendix string at the matching number, byte for byte (re-derived in verify_wang_2026_attitude.R by re-downloading the .docx). The same AT1/AT2/AT3 codes and wording appear in the upstream source the paper names, Ayanwale et al. (2022) doi:10.1016/j.caeai.2022.100099, with 'AI technology' in place of 'DG technology'. (B) The paper's Table 2 (image asset .t002) publishes loadings under the DATA's codes: ATT1 0.825, ATT2 0.815, ATT3 0.836, CA 0.766, CR 0.865, AVE 0.681. Recomputed from the S2 Appendix columns ATT1/ATT2/ATT3 (n=500, PLS mode-A single construct): 0.824 / 0.818 / 0.834, CA 0.766, CR 0.865, AVE 0.681 -- max loading deviation 0.003, reliabilities exact to 3 dp, and the rank order ATT3>ATT1>ATT2 matches, so the published codes sit on those columns in that orientation. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH, hence PARTIAL: (i) the appendix's prefix is AT<n> while the data's is ATT<n>, and nothing in the deposit states that correspondence -- it rests on the shared numbering and there being exactly one 3-item attitude construct; (ii) the three items are near-synonymous enjoyment items whose means (3.79 / 3.72 / 3.73), SDs (1.05 / 1.07 / 1.06) and loadings (spread 0.018) are inside estimation noise, so a permutation of the three wordings among the three codes is not detectable from the data by any route.
